title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching improved throughput but exposed a scheduling imbalance under skewed tenant mixes: low-volume customers could be starved by high-throughput streams and long-lived KV-cache warmups could delay small latency-sensitive requests. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to provide stronger queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and configurable timeouts while keeping throughput gains.

What this PR does (summary): implemented a multi-queue scheduler with aging-based priority promotion, per-tenant minimum service slices, and soft preemption for long-running batches. Introduced request-level queueing timeouts and backpressure signals that prefer warm KV-cache entries for latency-sensitive paths. Added detailed metrics and tracing hooks to measure queue wait percentiles, starvation incidents, and preemption counts. Provided a staged rollout plan behind a feature flag.

Key design points: 1) Multi-queue: requests are assigned to bins based on expected cost (short/long) and priority (interactive/batch). 2) Aging promotion: requests in low-priority queues are promoted over time to avoid indefinite starvation; promotion rate is tunable per-service. 3) Minimum service slice: each tenant is guaranteed a minimum number of scheduling slices per scheduling epoch to enforce fairness across tenants. 4) Soft preemption: when a long batch threatens latency SLOs, we allow currently queued short requests to preempt remaining batch capacity; the long batch will be split and requeued with adjusted priority. 5) Queueing timeouts: requests have configurable timeouts which trigger fallback policies (route to alternative model variant or return an early partial response). 6) KV-cache-aware routing: scheduler prefers requests with warmed KV-cache entries when nearing tail-latency windows to maximize useful work per GPU.

Testing and validation: unit tests for promotion and preemption logic; integration tests with synthetic tenant mixes; perf-canary harness that runs mixed workloads (10x heavy tenant, many small interactive tenants). Observability: added metrics (scheduler.queue_wait_p50/p95/p99, scheduler.starvation_incidents, scheduler.preemption_count, scheduler.promotion_rate) and tracing spans for queue lifecycle.

Rollout: behind feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2. Canary rollout to 10% of serving nodes for 48 hours with automatic rollback if p99 latency or starvation_incidents regress beyond thresholds.

Backwards compatibility: no API changes. Default behavior unchanged until flag enabled.

Notes: This PR focuses on scheduler behavior and tuning; kernel-level execution and quantization paths unchanged. Follow-ups planned for adaptive promotion rates driven by live telemetry and autoscaling integration.
commits: 3 commits: 1) Implement multi-queue scheduler core and aging promotion (author: Ava Chen) 2) Add preemption/slice logic, timeouts, and KV-cache routing hooks (author: Ava Chen) 3) Tests, metrics, docs, and rollout flag (author: Ava Chen)
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice design. Can you justify the chosen promotion half-life? Will this interact poorly with bursty traffic?

Ava Chen: The default promotion half-life is 200ms, chosen from canary runs; it's configurable per-service. Burstiness is addressed by the minimum service slice which ensures short requests see timely service even during bursts.
Priya Rao: Preemption looks promising but I'm concerned about requeue amplification for long-running batches. How do we bound requeue overhead?
Ava Chen: We add a requeue cap (max_requeues=2) and increase priority slightly on requeue to avoid thrashing. Added tests to validate worst-case requeue counts.
Liam O'Connor: Perf canary initially showed a small p99 regression for a specific long-sequence workload. Did you identify root cause?

Ava Chen: Root cause was the preemption threshold being too aggressive; tuned threshold to require at least 40ms of remaining long-batch work before splitting. Verified with canary that p99 now improves for interactive requests while long-batch throughput impact is <2%.
Diego Martinez: Approve after addressing minor nits in metrics naming and adding a comment on the promotion constant.
Ava Chen: Addressed nits and pushed follow-up commit to rename scheduler.promotion_rate -> scheduler.promotion_half_life_ms and added comment.

release_notes: Improves continuous-batcher scheduling fairness and prevents tenant starvation by introducing aging-based promotion, per-tenant minimum service slices, soft preemption for long batches, configurable queueing timeouts, and KV-cache-aware routing. Exposed behind feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2. No breaking changes.
notes: Follow-ups: 1) telemetry-driven adaptive promotion rates (ENG-2191) 2) integrate with autoscaler signals to adjust slices dynamically 3) extend KV-cache warmup hints to the model-loader layer.
